title: Lunchbox runtime todo clipboard — Arpita
content:
Quick dump while I eat — brain + small-ticket checklist. Not polished.

Local context: oncall handoff from Diego at 10:40; saw a couple of p99 spikes on small-seq models (seq_len ~128) after the new batch scheduler change. Replicated a tiny repro on my devbox (2xA100 sim).

Morning micro-triage (things to file/confirm):
- Repro: p99 jumps from 68ms -> 210ms when batch size transitions from 8->16 under low concurrency. Happens with kv-cache disabled; maybe cache eviction interaction. (JIRA-RT-2413)
- Kernel oddity: observed a 10-15% stall inside memcpy_gdr_copy path when NVLink device switching happens. Log snippet attached to PR 887.
- User-visible failure: one customer saw >1s first-token latency intermittently. Likely downstream of batching backpressure; need to check routing policy logs.

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Batching window extension + cache eviction race -> big wakeup cost when cache miss causes warmup. Test by forcing cache warm state and measure.
2) Kernel memcpy path uses fallback when alignment triggers slow path after small spikes in traffic; test with synthetic aligned workload.
3) Scheduler throttle mis-calculation under bursty arrivals (enqueue time distribution mis-estimated).

Immediate experiments (today, quick):
- EXP-1: run small-seq e2e with kv-cache pinned on and off, compare p50/p95/p99. Commands: 
  - ./tools/loadgen --model small-7b --seq 128 --concurrency 32 --duration 300 --kv-cache on
  - ./tools/loadgen --model small-7b --seq 128 --concurrency 32 --duration 300 --kv-cache off
  Record latency hist and kernel traces.
- EXP-2: add instrumentation to batch scheduler: log batch window start/end timestamps for each batch and avg enqueue delay. Quick patch in scheduler/logging. (small PR ok)
- EXP-3: perf hotspot: run linux perf on memcpy_gdr_copy for 60s during spike; collect flamegraph.

Quick triage checklist (done / next):
- [x] Grab node logs from 11/07 08:00-11:00 (done, in /tmp/arpita-node-logs)
- [x] Reproduce local p99 spike (done, repro saved at ~/repro/p99-spike-20241107)
- [ ] Push minimal instrumentation PR for scheduler (target: revertable, small)
- [ ] Run EXP-1 and upload histograms to S3 (s3://redwood-dev/arpita/exp1)
- [ ] Capture perf flamegraph and attach to JIRA-RT-2413
- [ ] If repro persists, schedule 30m async with Diego to review kernel traces

Kernel notes (raw):
- Observed: kcopy path triggers fallback copy when src/dst pointers not NV_P2P-friendly -> leads to extra memcpy staged through host. Might explain extra ~100us per token at scale.
- Hypothesis: CUDA peer mapping logic occasionally returns not-ready state when another process created a temporary mapping. Race? Check KMS/HIP context reuse.
- Quick check: run stress test with persistent peer mappings: 
  - export CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 && ./scripts/p2p-stress.sh 1000

Operational caveats:
- If we enable aggressive batching to flatten p99, watch memory pressure on KV cache (eviction thrash can make tail worse).
- For Dedicated customers, consider temporary routing to smaller-batched nodepool if they hit first-token > 500ms. Add to runbook as manual mitigation.

Notes to self:
- Keep PRs tiny; signal in title: [instrumentation][revertable]
- When filing kernel bug, include two things: minimal repro + perf samples (not only log lines). Kernel folks like perf data.

Loose TODO (someday):
- Add a per-request KV-cache hitrate metric exposed to console (would make diagnosing this class of regressions faster).
- Explore simpler fallback: if batch window would cause >200ms first-token, send as direct (no wait) and pay cost. Might be configured per-customer.

Conversations/links to follow up:
- Slack: #runtime-kernel thread "memcpy NVLink fallback" (pings: diego, minah)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/infer-runtime/pull/887 (instrumentation + repro logs)
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-2413 (p99 spike small-seq)

End-of-lunch plan: push scheduler logging PR, start EXP-1 run, and capture perf if spike reappears. If nothing reproduces, schedule deep-dive with kernel team tomorrow morning.

Random scratch: if I have time, try toggling the per-shard batch cap from 32 -> 24 to see if it reduces enqueue tail (cheap change).

-- arpita
